learn.hook: Two teams of number cards have different totals. One clever swap can make them equal. Can you find it?
points: First find the sum of each group.
Add both sums and halve the total. That is what each group must have.
Swapping card x from the bigger group with card y from the smaller group moves x − y across.
Choose x − y = half the difference between the two sums.
Try to use the fewest swaps. Often one good swap is enough, but sometimes no single swap works.

example.q: Group A: 9, 4, 7 (sum 20). Group B: 3, 5, 6 (sum 14). Find one swap to make the sums equal.
steps: A must lose 3, so x − y = 3
Swap 9 from A with 6 from B: 9 − 6 = 3

learn.reallife: Picking two kabaddi teams of equal strength is like making sums equal!

games.title: Swap check
items: Groups 8, 2 and 5, 1: swapping 8 and 5 makes the sums equal.
The sums become 7 and 9, not equal.
If the sums are 20 and 14, each group needs 17.
Swapping a 7 and a 5 moves 2 from one sum to the other.
One sum goes down by 2, the other goes up by 2.
Swapping two equal numbers changes the sums.

quiz.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. What should each group's sum be after swapping?
quiz.explain: A = 16 and B = 12. Total 28, so each needs 28 ÷ 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Takes the bigger sum

quiz.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. Which one swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A must lose 2, and 8 − 6 = 2. Now A = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 and B = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14.
steps: Sums: A = 8 + 3 + 5 = 16, B = 2 + 6 + 4 = 12. Total 28, so each needs 14.
A must lose 2, so swap x from A and y from B with x − y = 2: 8 − 6 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Swaps without checking the new sums

quiz.q: Two groups have sums 23 and 17. A swap moves x − y from the bigger group. What should x − y be?
quiz.explain: The difference is 23 − 17 = 6. Half of 6 is 3. Moving 3 makes both 20.
quiz.mistake: Moves the whole difference instead of half

quiz.q: Group A: 10, 3. Group B: 8, 1. Which swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 13, B = 9, each needs 11, so A must lose 2. 10 − 8 = 2 works. (Swapping 3 and 1 also works, but it is not listed.)
steps: Sums: A = 10 + 3 = 13, B = 8 + 1 = 9. Total 22, so each needs 11.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the new sums

quiz.q: Group A: 7, 6, 5. Group B: 4, 3, 1. What is the fewest number of swaps that makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 18, B = 8, each needs 13. A must lose 5. Swap 6 with 1: 6 − 1 = 5. One swap is enough.
steps: 18 + 8 = 26, so each needs 26 ÷ 2 = 13. A must lose 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big difference needs many swaps

quiz.q: Group A: 9, 2. Group B: 5, 4. Which single swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 11, B = 9, so A must lose 1. The swaps move 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5, or make A bigger. None moves exactly 1.
steps: Sums: A = 9 + 2 = 11, B = 5 + 4 = 9. Each needs 10, so A must lose 1.
Possible moves: 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5; swapping 2 makes A bigger.
No swap moves exactly 1, so no single swap works.
quiz.mistake: Assumes there is always a swap

quiz.q: After a swap, Group A went from 20 to 17. Group B was 14. What is Group B now?
quiz.explain: Whatever A loses, B gains. A lost 3, so B is 14 + 3 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Thinks both groups lose

quiz.q: Group A: 12, 5, 1 (sum 18). Group B: 7, 4, 3 (sum 14). Which swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: Each group needs 16, so A must lose 2. 5 − 3 = 2. Now A = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16 and B = 7 + 4 + 5 = 16.
steps: Total 18 + 14 = 32, so each group needs 16. A must lose 2.
Need x − y = 2 with x from A, y from B: 5 − 3 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Picks a swap without working out how much must move

teach.ask: Gappu has groups 6, 5, 9 and 4, 3, 7. How do I make the sums equal with one swap?
teach.praise: Each group needs 17. I swap 6 with 3 — A loses 3 and B gains 3. Done!
teach.nudge: What total should each group have?

revise.summary: To make two groups' sums equal, find each sum, add them and halve the total. Swapping x from the bigger group with y from the smaller moves x − y across, so choose x − y = half the difference.
focus: Find the target sum for each group
Find one swap that makes the sums equal
Know when no single swap works
remember: Target = (sum A + sum B) ÷ 2
A swap moves x − y from the bigger group to the smaller
Choose x − y = half the difference of the sums
traps: Don't move the whole difference; move half of it.
Don't swap without checking the new sums.
There is not always a single swap that works.

learn.hook: Adding 99 looks hard, but adding 100 is easy. Can you see the trick?
points: To add 99, add 100 and take away 1. To add 999, add 1,000 and take away 1.
To add 98, add 100 and take away 2. To add 198, add 200 and take away 2.
Round one number to the nearest ten, add, then adjust: 47 + 38 = 47 + 40 − 2 = 85.
When fuel is filled into a tank, add the new litres to what was already there.

example.q: A tractor tank had 136 litres of diesel. 99 litres more were filled. How much is in the tank now?

learn.reallife: Petrol pump attendants and shopkeepers add quickly in their heads using these tricks.

quiz.q: What is 456 + 99?
quiz.mistake: Adds 100 but forgets to take away 1

quiz.q: What is the easy way to work out 2,345 + 999?
quiz.explain: 999 is 1 less than 1,000, so add 1,000 and take away 1.
quiz.mistake: Adjusts in the wrong direction

quiz.q: Using 68 + 30, what is 68 + 29?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to adjust

quiz.q: A bus tank has 48 litres of diesel. The driver fills 37 litres more. How much is in the tank?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: A car used 18 L of petrol on Monday, 26 L on Tuesday and 24 L on Wednesday. How much in all?
quiz.mistake: Makes a carrying error
Adds the 2 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Which is the same as 345 + 97?
steps: So adding 97 = adding 100, then taking away 3.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 3 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: One fuel tanker carries 2,500 L and another carries 1,999 L. How much do they carry together?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take away the 1

teach.ask: Gappu must add 527 + 99 in his head. What trick can I use?
teach.praise: Add 100 to get 627, then take away 1: 626. So quick!
teach.nudge: Which easy number is 99 close to?

revise.summary: Add numbers near a hundred or a thousand the easy way: to add 99, add 100 and take away 1; to add 98, add 100 and take away 2. Round, add, then adjust.
focus: Add 99, 98, 999 or 198 quickly
Round one number to the nearest ten, add, then adjust
Add fuel or other amounts in real problems
traps: Don't forget to take away the extra 1 after adding 100.
Don't adjust in the wrong direction: 345 + 97 = 345 + 100 − 3, not + 3.

learn.hook: If 25 + 17 = 42, you already know two subtraction facts for free! Can you find them?
points: Addition and subtraction are inverse (opposite) operations. One undoes the other.
To find a missing number, use the opposite operation: ? − 245 = 380 means ? = 380 + 245.
learn.reallife: When a shopkeeper gives change, he often counts up from the price to the money you gave — adding to check a subtraction!

games.title: Partners
items: To find ? in ? − 50 = 20, we add 50 and 20.

quiz.q: From 345 + 128 = 473, which subtraction fact is true?
quiz.explain: Take away one part from the total to get the other part.
steps: In 345 + 128 = 473, the parts are 345 and 128; the total is 473.
Total − one part = the other part.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the wrong numbers

quiz.q: From 63 − 27 = 36, which addition fact is true?
quiz.explain: Add back what was taken away to get the start number.
steps: Add back what was taken away to get the start.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong pair

quiz.q: ? − 245 = 380. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: 512 − ? = 287. What is the missing number?
steps: Start − ? = what is left, so ? = start − what is left.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers

quiz.q: ? + 1,450 = 3,000. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Which operation undoes addition?
quiz.explain: Subtraction takes away what was added, so it undoes addition.
steps: Subtraction takes away what was added.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplication is the opposite of addition

quiz.q: Which is NOT in the fact family of 56 + 44 = 100?
quiz.explain: 56 − 44 is 12, not 100. The other three use the same three numbers correctly.
steps: The fact family of 56 + 44 = 100 uses 56, 44, 100 correctly.
56 − 44 = 12, not 100. So 56 − 44 = 100 is NOT in the family.
quiz.mistake: Does not check each fact

quiz.q: Ravi had some marbles. He gave away 38 and has 47 left. How many did he have at first?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the numbers

teach.ask: Gappu knows 48 + 27 = 75. Which subtraction facts can I write from it without working?
teach.praise: 75 − 27 = 48 and 75 − 48 = 27. Addition and subtraction are partners!
teach.nudge: What do I get if I take away one part from 75?

revise.summary: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations: one undoes the other. Use the opposite operation to find a missing number or to make a fact family.
focus: Write related facts from an addition or subtraction
Find a missing number in ? − a = b or a − ? = b
Solve 'how many at first' word problems
remember: Subtraction undoes addition
traps: Don't subtract when you must add back: ? − 38 = 47 means ? = 85.
Multiplication is not the opposite of addition.

learn.hook: Add 15 + 16 + 17 in two seconds? There is a magic shortcut using the middle number!
points: Consecutive numbers come one after another without skipping: 23, 24, 25.
The sum of 2 consecutive numbers is always odd, because one of them is odd and one is even.
The sum of 3 consecutive numbers can be odd or even. The sum of 4 consecutive numbers is always even.
Sums of 2 consecutive numbers go 3, 5, 7, 9 … (up by 2). Sums of 3 go 6, 9, 12 … (up by 3).
Shortcut: for an odd count of consecutive numbers, sum = middle number × count. 15 + 16 + 17 = 16 × 3 = 48.

steps: There are 5 numbers; the middle one is 23

learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a lane are often consecutive odd numbers — patterns are everywhere!

quiz.q: Which of these are consecutive numbers?
quiz.explain: 34, 35, 36 follow one after another with nothing skipped.
steps: Consecutive means one after another, nothing skipped.
34, 35, 36 has nothing skipped, so it is consecutive.
quiz.mistake: Thinks even numbers in a row are consecutive

quiz.q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is always…
quiz.explain: One number is odd and the other is even, and odd + even = odd.
steps: Of two consecutive numbers, one is odd and one is even.
So the sum is always odd.
quiz.mistake: Has not tried any examples

quiz.q: What is 15 + 16 + 17?
steps: 3 consecutive numbers; the middle one is 16.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the first number by 3

quiz.q: Is the sum of 4 consecutive numbers odd or even?
quiz.explain: 4 consecutive numbers have 2 odd and 2 even numbers. Two odds make an even, so the total is even. Example: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
steps: 4 consecutive numbers have 2 odd and 2 even numbers.
Odd + odd = even, and adding evens keeps it even.
So the sum is always even (e.g. 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10).
quiz.mistake: Tries only one example and guesses

quiz.q: Which is true about the sum of 3 consecutive numbers?
options: It can be odd or even
steps: So it can be odd or even.
Answer: It can be odd or even
quiz.mistake: Generalises from one example

quiz.q: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 5 = 9. By how much does each sum grow?
quiz.mistake: Thinks each sum grows by 1

quiz.explain: The sums grow by 3 each time: 12 + 3 = 15.
steps: The sums 6, 9, 12 grow by 3 each time.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 instead of 3

quiz.q: Find 41 + 42 + 43 + 44 + 45 + 46 + 47 using the middle number.
quiz.mistake: Picks the wrong middle number

teach.ask: Gappu must add 32 + 33 + 34 + 35 + 36. Is there a quick way?
teach.praise: The middle number 34 times 5 numbers is 170. Magic shortcut!
teach.nudge: Which number is in the middle, and how many numbers are there?

revise.summary: Consecutive numbers come one after another. Two consecutive numbers always add to an odd number, four always add to an even number, and for an odd count, sum = middle number × count.
focus: Spot consecutive numbers
Say if sums of 2, 3 or 4 consecutive numbers are odd or even
Add consecutive numbers using the middle number
remember: Sum of 2 consecutive numbers is always odd
Sum of 3 can be odd or even; sum of 4 is always even
traps: Even numbers in a row (34, 36, 38) are not consecutive.
Don't decide from one example; try a few.

learn.hook: Two trains together travel thousands of kilometres in a month. Can you add like a station master?
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
Add from the right. If a column makes 10 or more, carry 1 to the next place on the left.
To subtract, start from the right. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place.
Check a subtraction by adding: answer + the number taken away = the starting number.

example.q: A train covered 24,365 km in March and 18,790 km in April. How far did it go in both months?

learn.reallife: Railway staff add up tickets sold, and families add up the cost of a holiday trip.

games.title: True or false?
items: To add big numbers, we line up the ones digits.
Ones go under ones so each place is added to the same place.
When a column adds up to 10 or more, we carry 1 to the next place on the left.

quiz.q: Riya's school collected ₹12,450 on Monday and ₹8,675 on Tuesday for a fair. How much in all?
quiz.explain: 12,450 + 8,675 = 21,125. Remember to carry in the tens, hundreds and thousands.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry 1 to the next place

quiz.q: A train has 1,248 passengers. 379 get off at Bhopal. How many are still on the train?
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column instead of borrowing

quiz.q: Kabir's town has 45,320 people. The next town has 38,905. How many more people live in Kabir's town?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of subtracting, or slips while borrowing

quiz.q: What is 50,000 − 1?
quiz.explain: One less than 50,000 is 49,999. All the zeros become 9s after borrowing.
quiz.mistake: Changes only one zero, or adds 1 instead of taking away

quiz.q: 26,500 + ? = 40,000. What is the missing number?
quiz.explain: Find the missing part by subtracting: 40,000 − 26,500 = 13,500.
quiz.mistake: Adds 40,000 and 26,500 instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Meena's family drove 1,285 km to Jaipur, then 642 km to Agra, then 1,073 km back home. How far did they drive in all?
quiz.mistake: Drops a carry when adding three numbers

quiz.q: Arjun had ₹5,000. He spent ₹1,750 on books and ₹865 on shoes. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Gives the amount spent (₹2,615) instead of the amount left

quiz.q: Aisha worked out 63,210 − 27,480 = 35,730. What is the best way to check her answer?
options: Add 35,730 + 27,480 and see if you get 63,210
quiz.explain: Adding the answer to the number taken away should give back the starting number. 35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so she is right.
steps: Answer + number taken away should give the start: 35,730 + 27,480.
35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so add them and see if you get 63,210.
Answer: Add 35,730 + 27,480 and see if you get 63,210
quiz.mistake: Does not know that adding undoes subtracting

quiz.q: Riya had ₹3,500. She spent ₹1,280 on a school bag and then got ₹750 from her nani on Raksha Bandhan. How much does she have now?
quiz.explain: Spending takes money away and receiving adds it: 3,500 − 1,280 = 2,220, then 2,220 + 750 = 2,970.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the money received instead of adding it

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'How do I add two really big numbers without getting muddled?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Line up the places, add from the right and carry when it is 10 or more!
teach.nudge: Where do I write each digit? And what do I do when a column makes 10 or more?

revise.summary: To add or subtract large numbers, line up the places, work from the right, carry when a column makes 10 or more, and borrow when the top digit is smaller.
focus: Add and subtract 5-digit numbers with carrying and borrowing
Solve money and distance word problems
Check a subtraction by adding
remember: Ones under ones, tens under tens
Carry 1 when a column makes 10 or more
Check: answer + number taken away = starting number
traps: Don't take the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column; borrow instead.
Don't forget to add money received in a mixed problem.
Don't give the amount spent when asked for the amount left.

learn.hook: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It already has 6,450 kg on it. Can it take your 4,000 kg of mangoes?
points: To find two numbers whose sum is closest to a target, try the pairs and see how far each sum is from the target.
Rounding first helps you find good pairs quickly, then check with exact sums.
Space left = capacity − load already carried.
For many loads, add them first or subtract them one by one.
If the new load is more than the space left, it cannot be carried.

example.q: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It has 6,450 kg. How much more can it carry?

learn.reallife: Lift signs say 'Maximum 680 kg'. Drivers and lift operators always check the load.

games.title: Load check
items: A boat for 1,500 kg can carry 980 kg of people and 365 kg of bags.
A lift for 680 kg can carry 545 kg of people and a 150 kg trolley.
If a truck holds 8,000 kg and has 5,250 kg, it can take 2,750 kg more.

quiz.q: Which two numbers from 2,345; 4,780; 5,620; 3,150 have a sum closest to 8,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 8,000.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the first pair that is near

quiz.q: Which two numbers from 6,250; 3,480; 4,100; 5,890 have a sum closest to 10,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 10,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest number first without checking

quiz.q: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It already has 6,450 kg. How much more can it carry?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake

quiz.q: A lorry carries 8,500 kg of cement. It drops 2,750 kg at one site and 3,125 kg at another. How much is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one delivery

quiz.q: A boat can carry 1,500 kg. The passengers weigh 980 kg and their bags 365 kg. How much more can it carry?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to include the bags

quiz.q: A lift can carry 680 kg. People inside weigh 545 kg. Can a 150 kg trolley go in too?
options: No, it would be 150 kg too much
No, it would be 15 kg too much
Yes, there is 15 kg to spare
steps: Answer: No, it would be 15 kg too much
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the total with the limit

quiz.q: Which pair from 2,480; 2,610; 1,995; 3,050 has a sum closest to 5,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 5,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks the two numbers closest to 2,500 without checking

quiz.q: A goods wagon can carry 25,000 kg. It has 12,600 kg of rice and 9,850 kg of wheat. How much space is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract from the capacity

teach.ask: Gappu's cart can carry 500 kg. It has 320 kg of grain. How much more can I load?
teach.nudge: Which two numbers should I subtract?

revise.summary: To find the pair closest to a target, try pairs and see how far each sum is. Space left = capacity − load already carried; a new load must fit in that space.
focus: Pick two numbers whose sum is closest to a target
Find space left after one or more loads
Decide whether a new load can be carried
remember: Space left = capacity − load
Round first to find good pairs, then check exact sums
If the new load is more than the space left, it cannot go
traps: Don't stop at the first pair that looks near; check them all.
Don't forget any part of the load, like the bags.

learn.hook: Do you need the exact answer to know if ₹1,000 is enough for a trip snack? Often a smart guess is enough!
points: Estimating means finding a quick answer that is close to the real one.
To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: round down.
To round to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit in the same way.
Round the numbers first, then add or subtract. 4,872 + 3,195 is about 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000.
An estimate helps us check if an exact answer makes sense.

example.q: Estimate 4,872 + 3,195 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
steps: 4,872: hundreds digit is 8, round up to 5,000
3,195: hundreds digit is 1, round down to 3,000

learn.reallife: News reports say 'about 2 lakh people came to the mela'. Shoppers round prices to see if they have enough money.

games.title: True or false?
items: 47 rounded to the nearest ten is 50.
The ones digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so we round up.
349 rounded to the nearest hundred is 400.
The tens digit is 4, less than 5, so it rounds down to 300.
650 rounded to the nearest hundred is 700.
The tens digit is 5, so we round up.
An estimate is always exactly the same as the real answer.
An estimate is close, not exact.

quiz.q: Round 3,462 to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: The tens digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 3,500.
steps: Hundreds digit is 4, tens digit is 6
quiz.mistake: Looks at the wrong digit or always rounds down

quiz.q: Round 67,280 to the nearest thousand.
quiz.explain: The hundreds digit is 2, less than 5, so round down to 67,000.
steps: Thousands digit is 7, hundreds digit is 2
quiz.mistake: Rounds up every time, or rounds to the nearest hundred instead

quiz.q: Estimate 498 + 307 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.mistake: Works out the exact answer (805) instead of estimating

quiz.q: A train carried 3,890 people on Monday and 5,120 on Tuesday. Rounding to the nearest thousand, about how many in all?
quiz.mistake: Gives the exact total (9,010) or rounds 3,890 down

quiz.q: Riya has ₹1,000. She wants toys costing ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. Round each to the nearest hundred. Does she have enough?
quiz.mistake: Rounds ₹395 or ₹289 the wrong way

quiz.q: Which number rounds to 5,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?
quiz.explain: 4,725 has hundreds digit 7, so it rounds up to 5,000. 4,450 rounds to 4,000; 5,620 and 5,501 round to 6,000.
steps: Nearest thousand: look at the hundreds digit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number that starts with 5 rounds to 5,000

quiz.q: Estimate 612 − 289 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 289 down to 200, or gives the exact answer

quiz.q: A school needs 28 buses with 52 seats each. Round both to the nearest ten to estimate the seats.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 28 down to 20, or works out the exact answer (1,456)

quiz.q: Riya's estimate said ₹1,000 is enough for toys of ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. She now adds exactly. How much money will be left?
quiz.explain: Exact total: 212 + 395 + 289 = 896. ₹1,000 is enough, and 1,000 − 896 = ₹104 is left.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total cost instead of the money left

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I round 3,462 to the nearest hundred?'
teach.praise: Yay! Look at the tens digit: 6 is 5 or more, so it goes up to 3,500!
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at? And when do I go up or down?

revise.summary: Estimating gives a quick answer close to the real one. Round each number first, then add or subtract; an estimate helps check whether an exact answer makes sense.
focus: Round to the nearest hundred or thousand
Estimate sums, differences and products by rounding
Use an estimate to decide if money is enough
remember: Nearest hundred: look at the tens digit
Nearest thousand: look at the hundreds digit
5 or more: round up; less than 5: round down
traps: Don't give the exact answer when asked to estimate.
Don't think every number starting with 5 rounds to 5,000: 5,620 → 6,000.

learn.hook: 638 + ? = 1,000. Can you find the missing number in a flash?
points: Numbers that add up to 100, 1,000 or 10,000 are complements: 73 + 27 = 100.
To reach 1,000 from 638: count up to 640 (2), then to 700 (60), then to 1,000 (300). 2 + 60 + 300 = 362.
To subtract 9, subtract 10 and add 1. To subtract 99, subtract 100 and add 1.
To find what to subtract from 457 to leave 99, work out 457 − 99 = 358.
learn.reallife: Counting change from ₹1,000 or ₹500 uses complements every day in shops.

quiz.q: What must be added to 638 to make 1,000?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing error across zeros

quiz.q: 4,725 + ? = 10,000. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Takes each digit away from 9 or 10 wrongly

quiz.q: 73 + ? = 100. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Takes each digit from 10

quiz.q: What is 562 − 99?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 1 instead of adding it back

quiz.q: What is 845 − 9?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add 1 back

quiz.q: What is the easy way to work out 1,234 − 99?
quiz.explain: 99 is 1 less than 100. Taking away 100 takes away 1 too many, so add 1 back.
steps: Taking away 100 takes away 1 too many.
quiz.mistake: Adjusts in the wrong direction

quiz.q: 457 − ? = 99. What number must be taken away?
quiz.mistake: Adds 99 instead of subtracting

quiz.q: 503 − ? = 9. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu has to work out 734 − 99 quickly. What should I do?
teach.praise: Take away 100 to get 634, then add 1 back: 635!
teach.nudge: Which round number is 99 close to?

revise.summary: Complements add up to 100, 1,000 or 10,000; count up in jumps to find them. To subtract 9 or 99, subtract 10 or 100 and add 1 back.
focus: Find what to add to reach 100, 1,000 or 10,000
Subtract 9 and 99 quickly
Find a missing number that is taken away
traps: Don't subtract 1 after taking away 100; add it back.
Don't add 99 when finding 457 − ? = 99; work out 457 − 99.

learn.hook: Read 12321 backwards. Same! Numbers like this are called palindromes.
points: A palindrome number reads the same forwards and backwards: 121, 4,554.
Two-digit palindromes are 11, 22, 33 … 99. There are 9 of them.
Three-digit palindromes between 100 and 200 are 101, 111, 121 … 191. There are 10.
Grid puzzle: put 1 to 9 in a 3 × 3 grid so that each row grows left to right and each column grows top to bottom.
In such a grid, 1 must be in the top-left corner and 9 in the bottom-right corner.
learn.reallife: Some dates are palindromes too, like 12-02-2021 written as 12022021!

games.title: Grid and palindrome facts
items: In the growing grid, 9 can go in the top-left corner.
9 is the biggest, so it must be at the end of its row and column: bottom-right.

quiz.q: Which number is a palindrome?
steps: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
Read 4,554 backwards: 4-5-5-4, the same as forwards.
4,545 → 5,454, 5,454 → 4,545 and 4,455 → 5,544: these change, so they are not palindromes.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the first and last digits

quiz.q: How many palindromes are there between 10 and 100?
steps: 2-digit palindromes have both digits the same.
quiz.mistake: Counts 10 or 100 too

quiz.q: How many palindromes are there between 100 and 200?
steps: The middle digit can be 0 to 9: 101, 111, … 191.
quiz.mistake: Forgets 101

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit palindrome?
quiz.explain: 100 backwards is 001, so it is not a palindrome. 101 is.
steps: 100 backwards is 001, so 100 is not a palindrome.
The next number of the form 1_1 is 101.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 100 is a palindrome

quiz.q: What is the next palindrome after 1,221?
quiz.explain: 4-digit palindromes look like abba. After 1,221 comes 1,331.
steps: After 1,221 (a = 1, b = 2) the next has b = 3: 1,331.
quiz.mistake: Changes only the last digit

quiz.q: In a 3 × 3 grid of 1 to 9 where rows grow left to right and columns grow top to bottom, where must 1 go?
quiz.explain: 1 is the smallest, so nothing can be to its left or above it.
steps: Rows grow left to right and columns grow top to bottom.
1 is the smallest, so nothing can be to its left or above it.
So 1 must go in the top-left corner.
quiz.mistake: Puts 1 in the centre

quiz.q: In the same growing grid, where must 9 go?
quiz.explain: 9 is the biggest, so it must be last in its row and its column.
steps: It must be last in its row (right) and last in its column (bottom).
So 9 must go in the bottom-right corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 9 can go anywhere at the edge

quiz.q: Which number is NOT a palindrome?
steps: 1,231 → 1,321, which is different. So 1,231 is NOT a palindrome.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the outside digits

teach.ask: Gappu found the number 2,442. Is it a palindrome? How do I check?
teach.praise: 2,442 backwards is 2,442. It is a palindrome!
teach.nudge: What happens when I read it from right to left?

revise.summary: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. In a 3 × 3 grid of 1 to 9 where rows and columns grow, 1 is top-left and 9 is bottom-right.
focus: Check whether a number is a palindrome
Count palindromes in a range
Place 1 and 9 in a growing grid
remember: There are 9 two-digit palindromes (11 to 99)
There are 10 palindromes between 100 and 200 (101 to 191)
101 is the smallest 3-digit palindrome
traps: Don't check only the first and last digits: 1,231 is not a palindrome.
100 is not a palindrome.

learn.hook: 27 children play a game in pairs. Will someone be left without a partner?
points: A number is even if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Otherwise it is odd.
Even numbers can be put into pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always leave one over.
Even + even = even. Odd + odd = even. Odd + even = odd.
Adding 2 does not change odd or even: 7, 9, 11 stay odd; 8, 10, 12 stay even.

example.q: Without adding, is 135 + 247 odd or even?

learn.reallife: Houses on one side of many roads have odd numbers, and on the other side even numbers.

quiz.q: Is 3,457 odd or even?
quiz.explain: The ones digit is 7, which is odd.
steps: Odd or even depends on the ones digit.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the first digit instead of the ones digit

quiz.q: Which number is even?
steps: Only 5,678 ends in 8, so it is even.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the wrong digit

quiz.q: 27 children stand in pairs. How many are left without a partner?
quiz.explain: 27 is odd. 13 pairs make 26, and 1 child is left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number can be paired

quiz.q: Without adding, is 135 + 247 odd or even?
quiz.explain: Both numbers are odd, and odd + odd = even.
steps: 135 ends in 5: odd. 247 ends in 7: odd.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd + odd = odd

quiz.q: Without adding, is 246 + 135 odd or even?
quiz.explain: 246 is even and 135 is odd. Even + odd = odd.
steps: 246 ends in 6: even. 135 ends in 5: odd.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger number decides

quiz.q: Start at 51 and keep adding 2. Which number can you land on?
quiz.explain: 51 is odd, and adding 2 keeps it odd. 75 is the only odd choice.
steps: 51 is odd. Adding 2 does not change odd or even.
So every number you land on is odd.
88, 70, 64 are even. Only 75 is odd, so 75.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding 2 changes odd to even

quiz.q: Which sum is odd?
quiz.explain: 23 is odd and 40 is even. Odd + even = odd.
steps: 22 + 40: even + even = even. 21 + 43 and 23 + 41: odd + odd = even.
Odd + even = odd, so 23 + 40 is odd.
quiz.mistake: Picks a sum of two odd numbers

quiz.q: Why can 36 laddoos be put into pairs with none left?
quiz.explain: Even numbers split into pairs exactly: 18 pairs.
steps: Even numbers split into pairs with none left over.
36 ends in 6, so it is even.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that has nothing to do with odd and even

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if 999 + 1,001 is odd or even without adding. Can you teach me?
teach.praise: Both are odd, and odd + odd = even. So the sum is even!

revise.summary: A number is even if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, otherwise odd. Even + even and odd + odd are even; odd + even is odd.
focus: Tell odd from even by the ones digit
Say if a sum is odd or even without adding
Use pairs to explain odd and even
remember: Even numbers pair up with none left over
Even + even = even; odd + odd = even; odd + even = odd
Adding 2 does not change odd or even
traps: Don't look at the first digit; look at the ones digit.
Odd + odd is not odd.

learn.hook: A light switch is pressed 25 times. Is the light on or off? Odd and even can tell you!
points: To find coin combinations, start with the biggest coins and list the ways step by step.
A switch that starts off: after an odd number of presses it is on; after an even number it is off.
To read a table, find the right row and column. Subtract to find how much higher one value is.

example.q: Everest is 8,849 m and K2 is 8,611 m. How much higher is Everest?

learn.reallife: Mountaineers compare heights of peaks, and electricians know that two presses bring a switch back to where it was.

games.title: Switch and coins
items: A switch that starts off is on after 7 presses.
A switch that starts off is on after 10 presses.
10 is even, so it is off.
₹10 can be made with two ₹5 coins.
The fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5) to make ₹13 is 3.

quiz.q: In how many ways can you make ₹6 using ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins?
quiz.mistake: Misses the ways that use only ₹1 coins

quiz.q: What is the fewest number of coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5) to make ₹13?
quiz.mistake: Does not use the biggest coins first

quiz.q: A light starts off. Its switch is pressed 15 times. Is it on or off?
quiz.explain: Each press changes it. 15 is odd, so it ends opposite to the start: on.
steps: After an odd number of presses it is opposite to the start.
15 is odd and it started off, so it is on.
quiz.mistake: Thinks many presses always end off

quiz.q: A fan starts off. Its switch is pressed 20 times. Is it on or off?
quiz.explain: 20 is even, so it ends the way it started: off.
steps: After an even number of presses it is back to the start.
20 is even and it started off, so it is off.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up odd and even

quiz.q: Everest is 8,849 m and K2 is 8,611 m. How much higher is Everest?
steps: How much higher = bigger height − smaller height.
quiz.mistake: Makes a subtraction error

quiz.q: Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m and Nanda Devi is 7,816 m. What is the difference?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to borrow

quiz.q: Heights: Everest 8,849 m, K2 8,611 m, Kangchenjunga 8,586 m. Which two are closest in height?
quiz.mistake: Compares only the first digits

quiz.q: A climber reached a peak in 2018, after her 26th birthday that year. In which year was she born?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu's lamp is off. If I press the switch 9 times, is it on or off? How do I know without pressing?
teach.praise: 9 is odd, so the lamp ends up on. Two presses cancel out!
teach.nudge: Is 9 odd or even, and what does each press do?

revise.summary: List coin combinations starting with the biggest coins. A switch that starts off is on after an odd number of presses and off after an even number. Subtract to compare values in a table.
focus: Count ways to make an amount with coins
Find the fewest coins for an amount
Decide if a switch is on or off
Read a table and find differences
remember: ₹6 can be made in 5 ways with ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins
Starts off: odd presses → on, even presses → off
Everest 8,849 m − K2 8,611 m = 238 m
traps: Don't miss the way that uses only ₹1 coins.
Don't mix up odd and even presses.

learn.hook: The school Maths Mela printed 350 certificates, but 412 children took part. Uh oh! How many more are needed?
points: Surplus means extra. Shortage means not enough. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
Line up places carefully when adding or subtracting big numbers.
For savings, add the money saved each month.
For 'how many more' or 'by how many runs', subtract.

example.q: 350 certificates were printed for 412 children. Is there a surplus or shortage, and of how many?
steps: 412 is more than 350, so there is a shortage

learn.reallife: Event planners always count chairs, plates and prizes to avoid shortages!

quiz.q: 350 certificates were printed but 412 children took part. How many more certificates are needed?
quiz.explain: 412 − 350 = 62 more are needed. This is a shortage.
steps: 412 children need certificates; only 350 were printed.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: 600 badges were made for 548 children. How many badges are extra?
quiz.explain: 600 − 548 = 52 extra badges. This is a surplus.
steps: 600 badges for 548 children: more badges than children.
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake

quiz.q: Asha saved ₹1,250 in January, ₹980 in February and ₹1,475 in March. How much did she save?
quiz.mistake: Forgets a carry

quiz.q: A factory made 12,450 toys on Monday and 9,875 on Tuesday. How many more on Monday?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two days

quiz.q: Team A scored 287 runs and Team B scored 249. By how many runs did Team A win?
steps: Winning margin = winner's runs − loser's runs.
quiz.mistake: Adds the scores

quiz.q: A factory must make 50,000 shirts. It has made 36,780. How many are still to be made?
quiz.mistake: Makes errors borrowing across zeros

steps: Line up places and add from the right.
Tens: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Thousands: 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Ten thousands: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry
Borrows wrongly across the zeros

teach.ask: Gappu ordered 120 laddoos for 135 guests. Is that a surplus or a shortage? By how many?
teach.praise: 135 − 120 = 15, so I am short by 15 laddoos. I will order more!
teach.nudge: Are there more guests or more laddoos?

revise.summary: In mixed problems, decide whether to add or subtract. Shortage or surplus, 'how many more' and 'by how many runs' need subtraction; total savings need addition.
focus: Find shortage or surplus
Add savings over months
Subtract big numbers, borrowing across zeros
remember: Surplus means extra; shortage means not enough
For 'how many more', subtract the smaller from the bigger
traps: Don't add when the question asks how many more.
Take care when borrowing across zeros: 80,000 − 46,385 = 33,615.

learn.hook: A bus does 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. Can you find the distance in a day without a calculator?
points: To multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, write 1, 2 or 3 zeros at the end: 45 × 100 = 4,500.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it: 135 × 24 = 135 × 20 + 135 × 4.
Division shares a number into equal parts or makes equal groups.
Check a division by multiplying: 2,400 ÷ 8 = 300 because 300 × 8 = 2,400.
A remainder is what is left over. It is always smaller than the number you divide by.

example.q: A bus makes 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. How far does it go in a day?

learn.reallife: Travel agents multiply ticket prices by the number of people, and teachers divide children into buses for a trip.

quiz.q: A train ticket costs ₹1,245. What is the cost of 6 tickets?
quiz.explain: 1,245 × 6 = 7,470. Multiply each place by 6 and carry.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried digits

quiz.q: What is 48 × 100?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end: 4,800.
steps: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end.
quiz.mistake: Writes one or three zeros instead of two

quiz.q: 1,350 students go on a trip in buses. Each bus takes 45 students. How many buses are needed?
quiz.mistake: Drops a zero while dividing

quiz.q: A plane flies 850 km every hour. How far does it fly in 12 hours?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only by the 2 in 12 and forgets the 10

quiz.q: Harpreet shares 2,400 packets of rangoli colours equally among 8 shops. How many packets does each shop get?
quiz.mistake: Loses or adds a zero

quiz.q: What is 236 × 25?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by only the 20 or only the 5 and forgets to add both parts

quiz.q: Joseph packs 97 laddoos in boxes of 8. How many full boxes does he get, and how many laddoos are left?
quiz.explain: 8 × 12 = 96, so 12 full boxes. 97 − 96 = 1 laddoo is left.
quiz.mistake: Leaves a remainder that is bigger than 8, or ignores the remainder

quiz.q: A cricket stadium sold 3,250 tickets each day for 4 days. How many tickets were sold in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 instead of multiplying, or forgets a carry

teach.ask: Gappu scratches his head: 'How can I multiply 135 by 24? It is too big!'
teach.praise: Super! Split 24 into 20 and 4, multiply each, then add. 3,240!
teach.nudge: How can I make 24 easier to work with? And what do I do with the two answers?

revise.summary: To multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, add 1, 2 or 3 zeros. Split a 2-digit multiplier into tens and ones. Division makes equal groups; check it by multiplying, and the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
focus: Multiply by 10, 100 and 1,000
Multiply by a 2-digit number by splitting
Divide and give the remainder
Check division by multiplying
remember: Remainder < the number you divide by
traps: Don't forget the tens part: 850 × 12 = 850 × 10 + 850 × 2.
Don't leave a remainder bigger than the divisor.
Don't drop or add a zero when dividing.
